answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text: Lifetime quantification may be difficult as the grid will be changing in other ways, and it would be hard to say a project has the same effect on the grid year over year going forward. Therefore, we would agree with the proposal to just report avoided emissions each year.

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text: Accounting at the hourly level is very challenging. This could be good for assessing impacts of a new generation source – but how would it work for those taking action on the demand side? As an electric utility, we develop programs to help our customers lower their demand during peak hours or shift use from high demand to lower demand hours. As an aggregated effort, there should be allowances for using averages when incremental hourly changes are not able to practically be assessed.

answers.label: Why annual or lifetime reporting
answers.text: There is too much variability on the grid to assume that the change that is seen in marginal rates in a given hour of a given year would be true for the lifetime of a project. The grid will be changing in other ways, and it would be hard to say a project has the same effect on the grid year over year going forward. Therefore, we would agree with the proposal to just report avoided emissions each year.

Why selected tests should be included
answers.text: Encouraging disclosure about whether a program is required by law may be informative but should not prevent quantification of the benefits for a reporter’s efforts. You want to encourage participation and not make things so complicated that reporters are reluctant to engage.

answers.label: Additionality tests missing from the framework
answers.text: This appears to focus only on renewable energy projects and exclude battery projects, electric vehicles, demand response, energy efficiency, etc. All of these are important actions and would have avoided emissions associated with them.

answers.label: Claims possible under different test approaches
answers.text:
Any new methodology associated with avoided emissions should specifically supply the types of claims that can be made. For example, if a reporter is doing something that another reporter will capture in their GHG inventory performance, they may be “enabling” the avoided emissions.
What and how to disclose should be included in this methodology.

answers.label: Why that temporal granularity ceiling
answers.text: While high granularity can be an option, it should not be required as not all reporters will be able to access or manage that level of data. A maturity model should be used with disclosure requirements regarding what level of temporal granularity is used.

answers.label: Other approaches for assigning margin weights
answers.text:
There should be more coverage in the methodology for how to report other actions that may affect the grid such as batteries, EV charging, and demand reduction or time of day shifting. While the end-user gets the inventory benefit, there are other companies that provide products and services to enable these activities, and it would be good for them to be able to demonstrate these potential benefits.
In addition, more guidance around Net-Zero accounting methodology in general is needed.
